name: King of Edom
overview: The King of Edom was a male Edomite tribal leader during the time of the Exodus. He is notably recognized for being the recipient of messengers sent by Moses, indicating a significant interaction between the Israelites and Edom at that historical moment. His role is situated within the broader narrative of Israel's journey from Egypt to the Promised Land.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Edom' simply denotes his position as the ruler over the Edomite people. The name means 'king [of] Edom' and is a descriptive title rather than a personal name, reflecting his authority over the Edomite tribe.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that the King of Edom is a descendant of Esau, connecting him genealogically to the patriarch of the Edomites. Beyond this inferred lineage, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Edom's significance lies in his interaction with Moses during the Exodus, when Moses sent messengers to seek passage through Edomite territory. This encounter highlights the geopolitical realities faced by Israel during their wilderness journey and reflects the ongoing relationship between Israel and the Edomites, descendants of Esau. His role underscores the challenges and negotiations involved in God's providential guidance of His people.
